puzzles.name: Final Causal Graph
puzzles.description: Assemble a causal graph that keeps the letter writer(s), the trap-setter, and the killer as potentially distinct actors rather than one default identity.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Arranges the true underlying events into one continuous, single-actor story and pressures the player to treat the sequence as proof of a single cause.
puzzles.design_constraint: The final reconstruction must not force identification of the real killer; it should let the player conclude who created the surrounding narrative confusion versus who is actually responsible, while leaving some elements genuinely unresolved.

hypotheses.statement: The earliest letters were a genuine, single-author exposé about the Massie/Mary relationship.
The original letter writer and Ron's killer were the same person.
A separate individual exploited the confusion created by the letters to kill Ron and frame the letter writer.
A second, distinct voice began writing under the original letter writer's identity, escalating the threats beyond the original author's intent.
